title: ChatGPT and Claude for Coding
description: Learn how to use general-purpose LLM chat interfaces like ChatGPT and Claude to architect solutions, debug complex issues, and write code outside of your IDE.

data.text: Why Use a Web Chat for Coding?

IDE-integrated tools like Copilot and Cursor are excellent for writing lines of code quickly, but web-based chat interfaces like ChatGPT and Claude excel at a different set of tasks: system design, explaining unfamiliar codebases, brainstorming approaches, and getting unstuck on hard problems. They also tend to have longer context windows and more powerful reasoning capabilities.
Best Use Cases for Web Chat

data.title: Where web chat assistants shine:
items: Architecting new features before writing any code
Explaining a large code snippet you found on Stack Overflow or GitHub
Debugging complex issues when you need to share large error traces
Learning a new library or framework with guided explanations
Generating boilerplate for a completely new project
Brainstorming multiple approaches to a hard problem

data.text: Both models are excellent for coding, but they have different strengths. Claude tends to produce cleaner, more readable code and handles large context windows well, making it strong for analyzing large files. ChatGPT with its Code Interpreter (Advanced Data Analysis) is strong for data manipulation, visualization, and working with files directly.

cards.title: Claude (Anthropic)
cards.description: Strongest at reading large files, producing clean idiomatic code, and following detailed instructions. Claude 3.5 Sonnet is widely considered the best general-purpose coding model available.
cons: Requires separate IDE integration for in-editor use

cards.title: ChatGPT (OpenAI)
cards.description: Broad ecosystem with Code Interpreter, Advanced Data Analysis, and a wide range of plugins. Strong for data tasks and rapid prototyping.
cons: Code quality can be inconsistent across versions

data.text: Claude's Artifacts feature lets it generate complete, runnable files or mini-applications alongside the chat response. You can see the code, edit it, and even run it in some interfaces. ChatGPT's Advanced Data Analysis can execute code, create visualizations, and work with uploaded files. Both features transform chat from a text-only interface into a lightweight coding environment.

data.title: Prototype first, integrate later
data.text: Use web chat to prototype a small utility, data transformation script, or HTML component. Once it works in the artifact, copy the code into your project and adapt it. This is much faster than writing the first version directly in your codebase.

data.title: A practical workflow for using web chat in your development process:
items: Start a chat session and describe the feature or problem in detail
Ask for the approach first, before asking for code — "What is the best way to implement X?"
Request code incrementally — start with the data model, then the function, then the tests
Paste the generated code into your editor and run your existing tests
Iterate with the chat: paste any errors and ask for fixes

data.text: When pasting code into a chat interface, include enough surrounding context for the AI to understand dependencies and patterns. Paste the function you want help with, plus the types it uses and any related functions. A small snippet of well-chosen context is worth more than a massive dump of unrelated files.

data.title: Effective chat prompt for debugging
data.content:
Instead of: "My API is broken"

Try: "I have a Next.js API route at app/api/users/route.ts that uses Prisma to query a PostgreSQL database. When I call it with GET /api/users?role=admin, I get a 500 error with this stack trace: [paste stack trace]. Here is the route code: [paste code]. The Prisma schema for User is: [paste schema]. What could be causing the 500?"

data.title: Do not paste secrets
data.text: Never paste API keys, database credentials, tokens, or other secrets into a web chat interface. The AI does not need them to understand your code, and you will expose them to a third-party service. Replace sensitive values with placeholders like YOUR_API_KEY.

Use Claude Artifacts to quickly scaffold a frontend component, a data dashboard, or a small utility. Ask for an artifact that includes HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in one file. You can preview it instantly, iterate with follow-up prompts, and then port the final version into your project.

data.title: Web chat coding rules of thumb
points: Use for architecture decisions, explanations, and debugging complex problems
Share well-chosen context, not entire codebases
Iterate incrementally — ask for small pieces at a time
Use Claude Artifacts or ChatGPT Code Interpreter for rapid prototyping
